children: Xiaomi's shares rose sharply after its third-quarter results showed its resilient smartphone profitability despite rising memory costs, with management striking an upbeat tone on electric-vehicle deliveries for the next quarter
Its shares gained 6.8% to 28.30 Hong Kong dollars early Wednesday, equivalent to US$3.61, outpacing a 1% gain in the benchmark Hang Seng Index.

Xiaomi's smartphone gross margin narrowed to 9.2% from 11.1% a year earlier as rising memory chip prices pressured handset makers. Xiaomi, known for its budget phones, has gradually expanded its lineup of higher-end models and raised prices modestly.
"Fundamentally, Xiaomi continues to navigate the memory cycle well, with resilient smartphone gross margins deserving credit," Bernstein analysts said in a note.
Xiaomi's management expects smartphone margins to remain resilient, helped by an improved product lineup and competitive prices, HSBC analysts said.

Citi analysts said Xiaomi is also developing new products to help offset rising costs. They pointed to the company's expectations for EV deliveries to top 50,000 in November and December, helped by promotions for new models and a backlog of orders.
Like other automarkers, Xiaomi faces slowing demand in China's domestic market. Xiaomi plans to enter the European market in 2027 and has established an R&D and design center in Germany.
